$comment: PREDICATE VOCABULARY BENCHMARK — the decision boundary that normalize-entities.ts actually ships.
WHY THIS FIXTURE EXISTS. src/lib/rdf/normalize-entities.ts rewrites an incoming predicate IRI to an
existing one when cosine >= PREDICATE_MATCH_THRESHOLD (0.88). That constant gates a WRITE into the
user's graph, and until 2026-08-15 it was tested only against a hand-written mock vector table:
the test asserted the branching logic given assumed cosines and never measured what a real embedding
model returns. This fixture supplies the measurement.
Labels are given in the form normalize-entities.ts embeds them — labelFromIRI() strips the IRI path
and turns hyphens into spaces — so the benchmark scores the exact strings production scores.
TWO CLASSES, AND THE SECOND MATTERS MORE.
shouldMerge  — same relation, different words. Missing one costs a duplicate predicate; the review
queue still sees the fact, and predicate-manager can merge it later. Recoverable.
mustNotMerge — different relations that look alike. Merging one SILENTLY REWRITES a fact into a
different fact before a human ever sees it. Not recoverable, and not visible.
So a false merge is the expensive error, and the benchmark weights it accordingly.

shouldMerge.why: OBSERVED 2026-08-15: qwen3.6 emitted has-number-of-hearts 3; the golden set says has-heart-count 3. Same fact, scored as a miss AND a false positive.
Same count-vs-number-of drift as the observed pair, on a different attribute.
Plural noun standing in for an explicit count.
Pure orthographic drift — the easiest case any model must pass.
Plain-verb drift; small models reach for the everyday word.
Register drift within the same direction of the relation.
Domain synonym for the same role.
Technical synonym; both name the Linnaean binomial.
Verb-phrase vs has-attribute phrasing of one taxonomic rank.
Domain synonym: 'reproductive' and 'breeding' name the same strategy in biology writing, and a model picks whichever the source text used.
Verb synonym on a capability edge.
Range/occurrence phrasing for the same relation.

mustNotMerge.why: IDENTICAL SHAPE, different attribute. If a model scores string shape over meaning this is where it fails, and it fails silently.
Inverse roles. Merging these reverses the food chain — and normalize-entities has NO antonym guard.
Inverse direction of one relation. Merging reverses every edge that uses it.
One word apart, and the two names are routinely different strings.
Adjacent taxonomic ranks; near-identical phrasing, strictly different rank.
Bounds of one range. Merging collapses a range into a contradiction.

OBSERVED 2026-08-15 and previously mis-read as a vocabulary miss. It is not: has-blood-protein hemocyanin is a DIFFERENT, also-correct fact, not another word for has-blood-color blue. A valid extra, not a synonym.

The golden set uses both and means different things: a species' range (is-found-in mediterranean-sea) vs an institution's fixed site (university-of-otago is-located-in new-zealand). Merging erases a distinction the graph author drew.
Negation. The one case a prefix rule already catches in semantic-diff — included to check the embedding alone, without that rule.
Unrelated attributes sharing the has-X-range shape. Should be an easy reject; included as the floor.
Substring negation — 'ability' is a substring of 'disability', so any containment-based matcher merges them.
